text: The hair color pattern of each puppy in a litter is different because each puppy inherited: A) different information from both parents B) identical information from both parents C) different information from only the mother D) identical information from only the father
skill: genetics - inheritance of traits, variation among offspring

text: All dogs shed hair. Some breeds shed very little, others a lot. Shedding can occur year-round (due to natural hair cycles, varies by breed/age/diet) or seasonally (due to changes in daylight length and temperature). Which statement correctly describes the cause of shedding? A) only inherited traits B) only environment C) inherited traits and the environment D) neither
skill: biology - traits influenced by both genetics and environment

text: A model shows dog life cycle stages: number 1 -> Puppy -> number 2 -> Adult dog -> number 3 -> (back to Puppy, implying reproduction). Which table correctly identifies stages 1, 2, 3? Option A: 1=growth,2=reproduction,3=birth. Option B: 1=birth,2=growth,3=death. Option C: 1=birth,2=reproduction,3=growth. Option D: 1=reproduction,2=birth,3=death
skill: life science - organism life cycle stages (birth, growth, reproduction, death)

text: Students sealed 5g water + 5g iron filings in a container (empty container mass 25g), shook it, left overnight. Next day the filings changed from black to dark red, and the total mass (filings+water+container) was measured as 35 grams (unchanged from 25+5+5=35). What does this evidence show? A) matter is conserved when substances are mixed in a closed system B) thermal conductivity increases in water C) all substances experience a phase change when combined D) chemical reactions release heat within a system
skill: physical science - conservation of matter in a closed system

text: A table shows mineral properties: Magnetite (black, light does not pass through, magnetic, not soluble), Garnet (red, light passes through, not magnetic, not soluble), Quartz (white, light passes through, not magnetic, not soluble). To separate magnetite from a sand sample containing all three minerals, which method works best? A) measure light passing through B) mix with water and filter C) use a magnet to remove it D) remove particles with tweezers
skill: physical science - separating mixtures using differing physical properties

text: On a world map showing earthquake and volcano locations, most earthquakes occur: A) in the center of continents B) in the center of oceans C) along some boundaries where oceans and continents meet D) along all boundaries where oceans and continents meet
skill: earth science - earthquakes occur along some (not all) tectonic/plate boundaries

text: In a city with many old, non-earthquake-reinforced buildings: solution list - 1) reinforce brick buildings and repair foundations so they don't crack, 2) design interior walls to absorb forces and be less likely to fail, 3) only build new structures on shallow soil with bedrock underneath, 4) only build shorter new structures, 5) secure walls to roof and foundation in existing buildings to prevent weight transfer during shaking. Which two solutions would best reduce earthquake impact for the majority of current residents (not just new construction)? A) 1 and 2 B) 2 and 3 C) 4 and 5 D) 5 and 3
skill: engineering/earth science - solutions for retrofitting existing buildings vs new construction

text: A wild plant obtains energy from its non-living environment. Which row correctly identifies the source of energy and explains how the plant uses it? Row 1: Sun - energy converted into motion energy transferred to the plant. Row 2: water - energy from water transferred between the plant and an insect. Row 3: soil - energy from soil chemically combined into matter recycled by the plant. Row 4: light - energy is captured and converted into a form usable by the plant. A) Row 1 B) Row 2 C) Row 3 D) Row 4
skill: life science - photosynthesis, plants capturing light energy

text: Two butterfly species share a habitat and both need the same host plant to survive. Butterfly A completes four life cycle stages that repeat again within one year (multiple generations per year). Butterfly B completes only one life cycle per year. Which claim is supported? A) both have the same stages occurring at the same time of year B) both have different stages occurring multiple times during the year C) over one year, both have similar life cycle stages, but their growth rate (how many generations/cycles) is different D) over one year, both complete one life cycle and their growth rate is the same
skill: life science - comparing life cycle timing/generations between species

text: A nature preserve uses controlled burns (mimicking natural wildfires) to maintain a sandy ecosystem. Benefits of controlled burns include: eliminating invasive species, burning leaves/twigs covering the soil so seeds can grow, preventing large trees from taking over, and helping some seed pods open and release seeds. Which claim accurately describes how controlled burns affect a butterfly that depends on a specific low-growing host plant? A) the environment the host plant needs to grow is maintained by controlled burns, allowing food to be produced for the butterfly B) tall trees and thick underbrush survive after controlled burns and provide better habitat C) controlled burns destroy all plants and prevent host plant growth for years D) the habitat is enlarged because the butterfly needs to move to different locations
skill: life science - habitat management, ecosystem maintenance via controlled burns

text: Earth is tilted on its axis as it orbits the Sun. Compared to the amount of daylight at the North Pole on June 21 (summer solstice), the amount of daylight at the North Pole on December 21 (winter solstice) is: A) less, because Earth is tilted on its axis B) less, because Earth rotates on its axis C) greater, because Earth is tilted on its axis D) greater, because Earth rotates on its axis
skill: earth/space science - Earth's axial tilt causes seasonal changes in daylight length

text: Two balloons rubbed with wool cloth in the same direction, then hung near each other, move apart from each other. Which statement correctly identifies the result of rubbing the balloons with wool cloth? A) each balloon became electrically charged and moved away from the other B) each balloon became magnetic and moved away from the other C) the wool cloth transferred electric charge from one balloon to the other, causing them to move apart D) the wool cloth caused opposite magnetic properties in each balloon, causing them to move apart
skill: physical science - static electricity, like charges repel

text: A balloon rubbed with wool cloth is held near small pieces of paper on a table, and the papers move upward toward the balloon. Which statement explains why the pieces of paper moved toward the balloon? A) the sum of forces on the paper resulted in zero net force B) the forces on the balloon and paper were equal and opposite C) the force of friction on the paper pushed it toward the balloon D) the force exerted by the balloon (electrostatic attraction) on the paper was greater than the force of gravity on the paper
skill: physical science - electrostatic force can overcome gravity on light objects

text: A student wants to repeat an investigation (charged balloon attracting paper) using another balloon made of the same material, size, and color. Why should the student complete another trial of this investigation? A) to test the material and size of the balloon B) to check the reliability of the results of the first trial C) because repeating trials allows for less data to be considered D) because all scientific investigations must have only two trials
skill: scientific method - importance of repeated trials for reliability

text: A student rubbed a balloon with wool cloth and held it 10 cm from a metal can lying on a table. The can rolled toward the balloon. Which statement is evidence that energy was converted from one form to another in this investigation? A) the balloon was held near the can B) the volume of air in the balloon decreased C) the can moved across the table D) the can was positioned on top of a table
skill: physical science - motion as evidence of energy transfer/conversion
